nature.title: 1. Nature and Scope
paragraphs: OriginalSound HQ (hereinafter "the Application") is a local music player for Windows 10 and Windows 11. It reads and processes only the music files and system audio streams that you authorize on your own device.
The Application does not upload your music files, personal information, or playback history to any remote server. All data, except for local logs, remains on your device and is managed by you.

The Application is distributed in three forms: (i) the official pre-built version published on Microsoft Store under a "60-day free trial + paid license" commercial model; (ii) the source code published on the public GitHub repository (https://github.com/Johnwikix/original-sound-hq-player) under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 (AGPL-3.0); and (iii) test builds periodically published by Sennpei Studio as Pre-release assets on GitHub Releases, provided free of charge on an "AS IS" basis and intended for testing and evaluation only.

system.title: 5. System Component Interaction Risks
paragraphs: During operation, the Application interacts with the following Windows system components: registering a system tray icon, creating WASAPI audio sessions, reading and writing log and settings files under your user profile directory, and invoking WASAPI / DirectSound interfaces.

Audio driver interaction: Exclusive modes (WASAPI Exclusive, ASIO, DSD Raw / DoP) bypass the system mixer and communicate directly with the audio driver. They may conflict with third-party audio enhancement software (system-wide equalizers, virtual sound cards, spatial audio plugins), which can result in no sound, audio glitches, sample rate anomalies, or Windows Audio Service restarts.

Third-party beautification and enhancement tools: If you have software such as StartAllBack, Rainmeter, TranslucentTB, third-party antivirus, or system optimization / theme tools installed, they may modify the same system components (such as DWM composition, Shell hooks, file associations) and cause anomalies in the Application's window backdrop, tray icon, hotkey response, or drag-and-drop behavior.

If you experience system anomalies—such as audio silence, missing tray icon, unresponsive hotkeys, or the application window failing to stay on top—after installing, updating, or uninstalling the Application, please first collect logs from Settings → About → Log Path (%USERPROFILE%\Documents\OriginalSoundPlayer\Logs) and contact the developer for troubleshooting. Do not perform system-level rollbacks or reinstalls before the cause is identified.
